hail.text:
A low hull with too many men in it comes alongside without hurrying, which is its own kind of threat.

"Bound where, carrying what, and by whose leave?" The speaker's Akkadian is careful and bad.

choices.text: Say nothing and let the master handle it.
choices.unavailableNote: You do not have six shekels for the master's fee.
You have no seal to show them, and they would not believe a description of one.
You do not have ten shekels for the toll.
Your Akkadian is not quick enough to argue a toll.

choices.text: Keep your silver and work the rest of the crossing.

seal.text:
The seal is looked at, handed back, and not mentioned again. The patrol boat peels away toward the shore.

"That was worth more than the toll," the master says. "Try not to spend it all at once."

settled.text: The master speaks for you, briefly and without warmth, and takes his fee out of your purse for the trouble. The patrol boat turns away without ceremony.

paid.text: The silver goes into a bag that is already full. Nobody writes a receipt. The patrol boat turns away without ceremony.

argued.text: You argue the toll down to four shekels and pay it, and the patrol boat leaves before you can be asked to repeat the argument.

worked.text: The master speaks for you and then puts you to work: bailing, hauling, and holding a steering oar until your hands stop being yours. The patrol boat turns away without ceremony. You keep your silver and lose a day.

sources: Late Bronze Age maritime tolls and patrols, general
provenance.notes: Tolls and patrols are plausible; this encounter is invented.
